# tgcalls-js — full documentation (v0.7.1)
This file concatenates the whole documentation set for LLM ingestion.


<!-- ===== README.md ===== -->

# README

# tgcalls-js

**pytgcalls-style Telegram group-call wrapper for Node.js.** Stream audio, video,
and screen shares into Telegram voice chats using a GramJS-family client
([`teleproto`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/teleproto) / `telegram`) or
[`mtcute`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@mtcute/node), on top of the official
[`ntgcalls`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ntgcalls) native binding (the C++ WebRTC
core by the pytgcalls team — prebuilt binaries, no compiling).

[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js)](https://github.com/kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js/releases)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

> **Status: v0.6.0** — audio + video + presentation + idle + playlist/queue + recording + incoming P2P calls + mtcute.
> Verified end-to-end against live Telegram voice chats (audio, video up to
> 1080p60, and 40-minute idle presence) on Node 20+.

## Features

- 🎵 **Audio** from a file, direct URL, YouTube (via yt-dlp), or a custom shell PCM pipe.
- 📃 **Playlist/queue** — `play()` / `enqueue()` / `skip()` / `playOnHold()`; tracks auto-advance, hold music loops while the queue is empty.
- ⏺️ **Recording** — `startRecording()` / `stopRecording()`; records incoming call audio (native mix of all speakers) to wav/mp3/opus via ffmpeg.
- 📞 **P2P calls, both directions** *(verified live)* — `listenCalls()` answers 1-on-1 calls, `callUser()` places one; audio + video.
- ⏺️ **P2P recording** — audio, or video+audio muxed to mp4 (`record: {path}`).
- 🎬 **Video** from the same source (`video: {width, height, fps}`), camera or presentation channel.
- 🖥️ **Screen share** via `startPresentation()` / `stopPresentation()`.
- 🧍 **Idle presence** via `joinIdle()` — stay in a call with no media (stable on UDP-capable hosts).
- 🔌 **Client-agnostic** — auto-detects teleproto / GramJS / mtcute, or bring your own `MTProtoAdapter`.
- 🧯 **Typed errors**, injectable `logger`, queue-friendly `setSource()`, clean lifecycle (`leave` / `dispose`).
- ✅ **Offline test suite** — fake MTProto + the real ntgcalls native core, no Telegram credentials needed.

## Install

```bash
# Pin a tag for stability. npm 12+ blocks git dependencies by default, hence --allow-git:
npm install --allow-git=all github:kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js#v0.7.0
```

Requirements:

- **Node.js ≥ 18** (tested on 20 / 22).
- **ffmpeg** on `PATH` — required for every audio/video source.
- **yt-dlp** on `PATH` — only if you use `joinYouTube()`.
- A **user account** session (StringSession / mtcute storage). **Bots cannot join voice chats.**

`ntgcalls` ships prebuilt binaries for Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64.
If install skips the platform binary, see [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md).

## Quick start

### teleproto / GramJS

```js
import { TelegramClient } from 'teleproto';
import { StringSession } from 'teleproto/sessions/index.js';
import { TgCallsClient } from 'tgcalls-js';

const client = new TelegramClient(new StringSession(SESSION), API_ID, API_HASH, {});
await client.connect();

const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client });
await tg.join(-1001234567890, { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' });
// streaming… auto-leaves when the track ends (autoLeave defaults to true)
```

> The archived `telegram` package works identically — just change the two import
> specifiers back to `telegram` / `telegram/sessions/index.js`.

### mtcute

```js
import { TelegramClient } from '@mtcute/node';
import { TgCallsClient } from 'tgcalls-js';

const client = new TelegramClient({ apiId: API_ID, apiHash: API_HASH, storage: 'account.session' });
await client.start();

const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client }); // client type auto-detected
await tg.join(-1001234567890, { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' });
```

### Video, YouTube, URL, shell

```js
// Video from the same file (camera channel)
await tg.join(chatId, { kind: 'file', path: './clip.mp4' }, {
  video: { width: 854, height: 480, fps: 30 },
});

// Screen share (presentation channel)
await tg.join(chatId, { kind: 'file', path: './clip.mp4' }, {
  video: { width: 1280, height: 720, fps: 30 }, presentation: true,
});

// YouTube / any yt-dlp-supported site
await tg.joinYouTube(chatId, 'https://youtube.com/watch?v=…');

// Direct URL (radio stream, mp3, m3u8, …)
await tg.join(chatId, { kind: 'url', url: 'https://example.com/stream.mp3' });

// Custom shell command piping s16le 48 kHz stereo PCM to stdout
await tg.join(chatId, {
  kind: 'shell',
  command: 'ffmpeg -i song.flac -loglevel panic -f s16le -ac 2 -ar 48000 pipe:1',
});
```

### Events

```js
tg.on('streamEnd', async ({ chatId, source, willAutoLeave }) => {
  // play the next track without leaving:
  await tg.setSource(chatId, { kind: 'file', path: './next.mp3' });
});
tg.on('connectionChange', (chatId, state) => { /* numeric ConnectionState */ });
```

**For AI agents / LLM tooling:** [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) (concise index) and
[`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) (full documentation in one file).
Coding agents working on this repo: see [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

## API at a glance

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `join(chat, source, opts?)` | Join a voice chat and stream a source |
| `joinYouTube(chat, url, opts?)` | Resolve via yt-dlp, then `join` |
| `joinIdle(chat, opts?)` | Join with no media (idle presence) |
| `startPresentation(chat, source, video?)` / `stopPresentation(chat)` | Screen-share channel |
| `setSource(chat, source)` | Swap the audio of an active call (queue) |
| `pause / resume / mute / unmute(chat)` | Native media controls |
| `time(chat)` | Seconds streamed |
| `leave(chat)` / `dispose()` | Leave one call / tear down everything |
| `activeCalls() / getCall(chat) / isActive(chat)` | Introspection |
| `resolveChatId(chat)` | username / t.me link / id → marked id |
| `on(event, cb)` | `streamEnd`, `connectionChange`, `update` |

Full signatures and types: [API reference](docs/api.md).

## How it works

```
channels.getFullChannel ──► full_chat.call (InputGroupCall)
ntgcalls.createCall ──────► native join params (JSON: ufrag/pwd/fp/ssrc)
ntgcalls.setStreamSources ─ ffmpeg/yt-dlp PCM source (SHELL)
phone.joinGroupCall ──────► UpdateGroupCallConnection.params (connect JSON)
ntgcalls.connect ─────────► WebRTC → Telegram media servers
```

Telegram's connect params are passed to the native core verbatim. The audio SSRC
used for `phone.leaveGroupCall` comes from the join params produced by
`ntgcalls.createCall`.

## Caveats

- `ntgcalls` is pinned to an exact `3.0.x` (currently `3.0.7`); the 3.x line is young and may shift upstream.
- Using `telegram` **and** `teleproto` in one process? Pass the matching `Api` namespace to each `TgCallsClient`. mtcute uses its own TL schema and needs no `Api`.
- `process.exit()` immediately after using the native lib can abort during WebRTC teardown (cosmetic; long-running bots are unaffected). `await tg.dispose()` first.
- Presentation requires an RTC connection — unavailable on UDP-blocked hosts in RTMP/STREAM mode.

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm run build          # tsc → dist/
npm run typecheck:all  # src + examples + test
npm test               # offline suite (no credentials)
npm run smoke          # verify dist exports
```

See [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) for conventions and pitfalls.

MIT for this wrapper. [`ntgcalls`](https://github.com/pytgcalls/ntgcalls) is
LGPL-3.0 (its own repo, installed as a dependency).

# Getting started

# Getting started

## Requirements

| Need | Why |
|---|---|
| Node.js ≥ 18 | runtime (tested on 20 / 22) |
| `ffmpeg` on PATH | decodes every audio/video source to PCM/rawvideo |
| `yt-dlp` on PATH | only for `joinYouTube()` / `resolveYouTube()` |
| A **user** account session | Telegram does not allow bots to join voice chats |
| `api_id` / `api_hash` | from <https://my.telegram.org> |

Install ffmpeg:

```bash
sudo apt-get install ffmpeg        # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp         # macOS
```

## Install the package

```bash
npm install --allow-git=all github:kotakbiasa/tgcalls-js#v0.7.0
```

npm 12+ blocks git dependencies by default (`EALLOWGIT`); `--allow-git=all`
opts in for this install.

`ntgcalls` provides prebuilt native binaries (Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64,
Windows x64). If your npm version skips the platform binary when installing from
a git URL, install it manually — see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

## Get a user session

You need a logged-in **user** client. Two common paths:

### teleproto / GramJS (StringSession)

```js
import { TelegramClient } from 'teleproto';
import { StringSession } from 'teleproto/sessions/index.js';

const client = new TelegramClient(new StringSession(''), API_ID, API_HASH, {});
await client.start({
  phoneNumber: async () => '+62…',
  phoneCode:   async () => /* code from the Telegram app */,
  password:    async () => /* 2FA password if enabled */,
});
const sessionString = client.session.save(); // store this securely, reuse later
```

Reuse it next time with `new StringSession(sessionString)` + `await client.connect()`.

### mtcute

```js
import { TelegramClient } from '@mtcute/node';
const client = new TelegramClient({ apiId: API_ID, apiHash: API_HASH, storage: 'account.session' });
await client.start({ phone: () => '+62…', code: () => /* … */, password: () => /* … */ });
```

> Keep session strings and 2FA passwords secret (e.g. a `chmod 600` file or a
> secrets manager). Never commit them.

## First stream

```js
import { TgCallsClient } from 'tgcalls-js';

const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client });

tg.on('connectionChange', (chatId, state) => console.log('state:', state));
tg.on('streamEnd', ({ chatId }) => console.log('track finished in', chatId));

// chat accepts a marked id (-100…), @username, or t.me link
await tg.join(-1001234567890, { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' });
```

The call auto-leaves when the track ends (`autoLeave` defaults to `true`). To keep
the call open and queue more tracks, set `autoLeave: false` and use `setSource()`
inside `streamEnd`.

## Verify your setup (no credentials)

```bash
npm test     # offline suite: fake MTProto + real ntgcalls core
npm run smoke
```

Next: the [Guide](guide.md) for video, presentation, idle, and adapters, or the
[API reference](api.md).


<!-- ===== docs/guide.md ===== -->

# Guide

# Guide

## The join flow

Every join follows the same ordered sequence (do not reorder it):

1. `channels.getFullChannel` (or `messages.getFullChat` for basic groups) → `fullChat.call` (InputGroupCall).
2. `ntgcalls.createCall(chatId)` → native join params JSON (contains the **ssrc**).
3. `ntgcalls.setStreamSources(chatId, CAPTURE, …)` — set media **before** the MTProto join so it flows immediately.
4. `phone.joinGroupCall(params)` → wait for `UpdateGroupCallConnection`.
5. `ntgcalls.connect(chatId, connParams)` → media starts.

The same join-params string is sent in `JoinGroupCall`, and its ssrc is reused for
`LeaveGroupCall`. The library handles all of this; you only call `join()`.

## Sources

`AudioSource` is one of:

```ts
{ kind: 'file'; path: string }                 // any ffmpeg-readable file
{ kind: 'url'; url: string; audioUrl?: string } // direct media URL; audioUrl for split video/audio
{ kind: 'shell'; command: string }              // command piping s16le 48kHz stereo PCM to stdout
```

- **file / url** are decoded by ffmpeg to PCM (`-f s16le -ac 2 -ar 48000 pipe:1`).
- **shell** gives you full control; the command must output raw PCM at 48 kHz stereo.
- `joinYouTube()` resolves a page URL to a direct media URL via yt-dlp, then joins.
  With video it requests separate `bestvideo + bestaudio` streams (`audioUrl` carries the audio).

## Video

Pass `video` to `join()` to stream video from the same file/URL:

```js
await tg.join(chatId, { kind: 'file', path: './clip.mp4' }, {
  video: { width: 854, height: 480, fps: 30 },
});
```

- Dimensions are probed and kept **even** (YUV420p requirement); scaling is proportional.
- `video: false` disables video; omitting it streams audio only.
- Start at 854×480@30 on small VPS; raise to 720p60 / 1080p60 if the host keeps up
  (verified stable on a 4-vCPU cloud VM).
- For YouTube video, prefer `vp9`/`avc1` over AV1 (AV1 is too heavy to decode in real time).

### Camera vs presentation

- `video` alone → **camera** channel.
- `presentation: true` (or `startPresentation()`) → **screen-share** channel.
- Camera and screen **cannot be active at the same time** in one call; starting a
  presentation replaces the camera channel.

```js
await tg.startPresentation(chatId, { kind: 'file', path: './slides.mp4' }, { width: 1280, height: 720 });
await tg.stopPresentation(chatId); // call stays, camera can resume
```

> `setStreamSources` **replaces** all devices: any device omitted from a description
> is dropped. The library rebuilds the video channel on `setSource()` so video is not
> silently lost when you swap audio.

## Idle presence

`joinIdle()` joins with no media — useful for a bot that waits in a voice chat:

```js
await tg.joinIdle(chatId, { autoLeave: false });
```

- On UDP-capable hosts this is stable indefinitely (verified: **40+ minutes**, no disconnect).
- On UDP-blocked hosts, a regular RTC join gets ICE-timeout-kicked after ~25s. With
  `allowCreate: true`, `joinIdle()` creates a missing call in **RTMP-stream** mode and
  joins muted; an existing call is not converted.

## Queue / swapping tracks

Built-in playlist (v0.4.0): queue tracks and they advance automatically when each
one ends — no manual `streamEnd` wiring needed.

```js
const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client });
await tg.play(chatId, first);          // join + start now
await tg.enqueue(chatId, second);      // play after first
await tg.then(chatId, third);          // alias of enqueue
await tg.playOnHold(chatId, holdLoop); // looped while the queue is empty

// later, from a command handler:
await tg.skip(chatId);                 // jump to the next track
tg.getCurrent(chatId);                 // the playing source
tg.getQueue(chatId);                   // queued sources (copy)
await tg.clearQueue(chatId);           // empty queue + hold
```

The call stays open while tracks are queued; it only auto-leaves when the queue
**and** hold are empty. `skip()` with nothing queued pauses playback (call stays).

For manual control, `setSource()` swaps the audio without leaving and keeps the
video channel intact:

```js
tg.on('streamEnd', async ({ chatId }) => {
  const next = queue.shift();
  if (next) await tg.setSource(chatId, next);
});
await tg.join(chatId, first, { autoLeave: false });
```

With `autoLeave: true` and **no** `streamEnd` handler (and no playlist), the call
auto-leaves when the stream ends.

## Recording

Record incoming call audio (what other participants say) to a file:

```js
await tg.join(chatId, music, { autoLeave: false });
await tg.startRecording(chatId, './call.wav');        // or .mp3 / .opus
// ... later
const path = await tg.stopRecording(chatId);          // finalizes the file
tg.isRecording(chatId);                               // false now
```

ntgcalls mixes all remote speakers natively and pipes PCM to ffmpeg, which encodes
to the path (container from the extension). Options: `{ sampleRate: 48000, channels: 1 }`.
One recording per chat; starting again replaces it. Leaving the call stops it too.
After `stopRecording`, give ffmpeg a moment to finalize before reading the file.

## P2P calls (incoming)

> **✅ Verified live** (0.7.0): the call reaches ICE `CONNECTED` and audio is heard
> by the caller. Requires a GramJS/teleproto client.

Answer incoming 1-on-1 voice calls and stream audio into them (e.g. a voice bot):

```js
await tg.listenCalls({
  source: { kind: 'file', path: './song.mp3' },
  onIncoming: ({ userId }) => { console.log('call from', userId); return true; },
});
// ... later
await tg.stopListeningCalls();
```

The DH key exchange and WebRTC engine run in ntgcalls; tgcalls-js orchestrates the
MTProto signaling (`phone.acceptCall`, signaling relay, teardown on hangup).
Requires a GramJS/teleproto client. `autoAccept` defaults to true; `onIncoming` can
reject specific callers. Outgoing calls and multi-party conference are follow-up work.

## Events

| Event | Payload | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `streamEnd` | `{ chatId, source, willAutoLeave }` | fires once per playback; with video, waits for both audio and video to end |
| `connectionChange` | `(chatId, state)` | `state` is a numeric `ConnectionState` (see below) |
| `update` | raw TL update | pass-through of group-call-related updates |

`ConnectionState` (numeric enum from ntgcalls):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | CONNECTING |
| 2 | CONNECTED |
| 4 | FAILED |
| 8 | TIMEOUT |
| 16 | CLOSED |

A handler that throws/rejects is logged (via the `logger` option) and never crashes
the process. Multiple handlers per event all run (registration order); `on`/`once`
return an unsubscribe function and `off` removes one. Registering any `streamEnd`
handler suppresses auto-leave.

## Adapters / client detection

`TgCallsClient` auto-detects the client:

- **mtcute** — has `.call` + `.onRawUpdate.add` → `MtcuteAdapter`.
- **GramJS / teleproto** — has `.invoke` → `GramjsAdapter`.
- **custom** — pass an object implementing `MTProtoAdapter` (`isAdapter: true`).

```js
import { GramjsAdapter, MtcuteAdapter, createAdapter } from 'tgcalls-js';
const adapter = createAdapter(client, { Api }); // or new GramjsAdapter(client, { Api })
const tg = new TgCallsClient({ client: adapter });
```

When mixing `telegram` and `teleproto` in one process, pass the matching `Api`
namespace per client to avoid ambiguous TL auto-detection. mtcute needs no `Api`.

> mtcute TL `Long` objects (low/high) are preserved **by reference** — do not convert
> them to JS bigint. GramJS/teleproto use plain bigint.

## Lifecycle & cleanup

- `leave(chat)` stops the native call and sends `LeaveGroupCall` (best-effort both).
- A failed `join()` cleans up the native call and leaves any zombie participant.
- On native `CLOSED`/`FAILED`, the library leaves via MTProto **before** notifying
  listeners, so you can safely destroy the MTProto client from the callback.
- `await tg.dispose()` before disposing the MTProto client; avoid `process.exit()`
  immediately after native use (WebRTC teardown can abort).

## Typed errors

```js
import { AlreadyInCallError, NoVoiceChatError, TgCallsError } from 'tgcalls-js';
try {
  await tg.join(chatId, src);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof AlreadyInCallError) console.log('busy in', e.chatId);
  else if (e instanceof NoVoiceChatError) console.log('start a voice chat first');
}
```

All library errors extend `TgCallsError` (which extends `Error`). See the
[API reference](api.md#errors).


<!-- ===== docs/api.md ===== -->

# API reference

# API reference

All exports come from the package root (`import … from 'tgcalls-js'`).

## `TgCallsClient`

### Constructor

```ts
new TgCallsClient(options: TgCallsOptions)
```

#### `TgCallsOptions`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `client` | `MTProtoLike \| MtcuteLike \| MTProtoAdapter` | — | teleproto/GramJS client, mtcute client, or a custom adapter |
| `Api` | `unknown` | auto | TL API namespace; pass per client when mixing `telegram` + `teleproto` |
| `ffmpegPath` | `string` | `"ffmpeg"` | ffmpeg binary |
| `ffprobePath` | `string` | `"ffprobe"` | ffprobe binary |
| `ytDlpPath` | `string` | `"yt-dlp"` | yt-dlp binary |
| `logger` | `{ error(...args: unknown[]): void }` | `console.error` | sink for internal warnings (e.g. a throwing event handler) |

### Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ntg` | `NTgCalls` | the underlying native instance (advanced use) |

### Methods

#### Joining

```ts
join(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
joinYouTube(chat: ChatRef, url: string, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
joinIdle(chat: ChatRef, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
resolveYouTube(url: string, video?: boolean): Promise<string | null>
```

- `join` — join the voice chat and stream `source`. Throws `AlreadyInCallError` if
  already in a call (or mid-join) in that chat.
- `joinYouTube` — resolve `url` via yt-dlp, then `join`.
- `joinIdle` — join with no media. With `allowCreate: true`, creates a missing call
  in RTMP-stream mode (for UDP-blocked hosts); an existing call is not converted.
  Throws `NoVoiceChatError` if there is no call and `allowCreate` is not set.
- `resolveYouTube` — resolve a page URL to a direct media URL (or `null`).

#### Presentation (screen share)

```ts
startPresentation(chat: ChatRef, source: Exclude<AudioSource, {kind:'shell'}>, video?: VideoOptions): Promise<void>
stopPresentation(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>
```

`startPresentation` joins the presentation channel with a file/url video source
(replaces the camera channel). `stopPresentation` leaves the presentation channel;
the call stays.

#### Playback control

```ts
setSource(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource): Promise<void>  // swap audio, keep video (queue)
pause(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
resume(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
mute(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
unmute(chat: ChatRef): Promise<boolean>
time(chat: ChatRef): Promise<number>                          // seconds streamed
```

#### Playlist / queue

```ts
play(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource, options?: JoinOptions): Promise<JoinResult>
enqueue(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource): Promise<void>   // alias: then()
then(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource): Promise<void>
skip(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>
playOnHold(chat: ChatRef, source: AudioSource | null): Promise<void>
clearQueue(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>
getCurrent(chat: ChatRef): AudioSource | null                // sync
getQueue(chat: ChatRef): AudioSource[]                       // sync; copy
```

- `play` — join (if not already in a call) and start `source` now, replacing the
  current track. The call is kept open (`autoLeave` off) so the playlist decides
  when to leave.
- `enqueue` / `then` — queue a track after the current one. Joins if no call is
  active; starts immediately if the call is idle; otherwise appends to the queue.
- `skip` — jump to the next queued track (or the hold track). With nothing queued,
  pauses playback (the call stays open).
- `playOnHold` — set a track looped while the queue is empty (hold music); `null` clears it.
- `clearQueue` — empty the queue and clear the hold track (current track keeps playing).
- `getCurrent` / `getQueue` — inspect the playing track and queued tracks (sync;
  numeric id or previously-resolved alias).

When a track ends, the next queued track (or the hold loop) starts automatically.
The call only auto-leaves when the queue **and** hold are empty (and `autoLeave` is
on with no `streamEnd` handler). The lower-level `setSource()` still works for
manual swapping.

#### Recording

```ts
startRecording(chat: ChatRef, path: string, options?: RecordOptions): Promise<RecordingInfo>
stopRecording(chat: ChatRef): Promise<string | null>   // returns the recorded path
getRecording(chat: ChatRef): RecordingInfo | null      // sync
isRecording(chat: ChatRef): boolean                    // sync
```

Records **incoming** call audio (what other participants say). ntgcalls mixes all
remote speakers natively and pipes s16le PCM to ffmpeg, which encodes to `path` —
the container is inferred from the extension (`.wav`, `.mp3`, `.opus`, …).
`RecordOptions`: `sampleRate` (default 48000), `channels` (default 1 mono).

Requires an active call. One recording per chat; calling `startRecording` again
replaces it. `stopRecording` closes the native writer, which SIGTERMs ffmpeg so the
container finalizes cleanly — allow a moment before reading the file. Leaving the
call also stops any recording.

#### P2P calls (incoming)

> **✅ Verified live** (tgcalls-js 0.7.0): incoming 1-on-1 calls connect and stream
> audio end-to-end (ICE `CONNECTED`, RTP flowing, audio heard by the caller).
>
> Notes for implementers:
> - Byte parameters passed to the ntgcalls binding must be **plain JS arrays**
>   (`Array.from(buf)`); `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` throw `An array was expected`.
>   The wrapper does this for you.
> - Signaling must use **V2 external signaling** (`8.0.0`/`9.0.0`). Passing
>   `12.0.0`/`13.0.0` makes ntgcalls route signaling over an SCTP data channel and
>   the call times out. `listenCalls` restricts the version list automatically.
> - Set `debug: true` to log per-step signaling/ICE diagnostics.

```ts
listenCalls(options: ListenCallsOptions): Promise<void>
stopListeningCalls(): Promise<void>
activeCallPeers(): bigint[]
```

`listenCalls` answers incoming 1-on-1 voice calls and streams `options.source` into
them. `ListenCallsOptions`: `source` (AudioSource), `autoAccept` (default true),
`onIncoming({userId, callId}) => boolean` (gate to accept/reject), `ffmpegPath`,
`debug` (verbose `[p2p]` signaling/ICE logs, default false), `logger`. The DH exchange + WebRTC run in ntgcalls; the library handles the MTProto
signaling. Requires a GramJS/teleproto client. One listener per client; calling
again replaces it. `stopListeningCalls` hangs up active calls.

#### Outgoing calls

```ts
callUser(userId: ChatRef, options?: { video?: boolean | VideoOptions }): Promise<bigint>
```

Calls `userId` and streams the same `source` into the call once the callee answers.
Requires `listenCalls()` first — that installs the update handler which drives the
accept → confirm steps. Returns the Telegram call id. The call is hung up by
`stopListeningCalls()` / `dispose()`, or when the peer ends it.

```ts
await tgcalls.listenCalls({ source: { kind: 'file', path: 'song.mp3' }, video: { width: 640, height: 360, fps: 25 } });
const callId = await tgcalls.callUser(123456789n, { video: true });
```

How it works: `initExchange` is called with a `null` gaHash so the native core
returns `SHA256(g_a)` for `phone.requestCall`; on `PhoneCallAccepted` the library
calls `exchangeKeys(gB, 0)` (the native core computes the fingerprint) and then
`phone.confirmCall(gA, keyFingerprint)`. `phone.requestCall` returns
`USER_PRIVACY_RESTRICTED` when the callee only accepts calls from contacts.

Multi-party conference is not yet supported.

#### Lifecycle

```ts
leave(chat: ChatRef): Promise<void>   // ntgcalls.stop + phone.leaveGroupCall (best-effort)
dispose(): Promise<void>              // stop all calls + detach update handlers; await before disposing the MTProto client
```

#### Introspection

```ts
activeCalls(): bigint[]                       // marked ids of all active calls
getCall(chat: ChatRef): ActiveCall | null     // sync; numeric id or previously-resolved alias
isActive(chat: ChatRef): boolean              // sync; same alias rules
resolveChatId(chat: ChatRef): Promise<bigint> // username / t.me link / id → marked id
```

#### Events

```ts
on<K extends keyof TgCallsEvents>(event: K, handler: TgCallsEvents[K]): () => void
off<K extends keyof TgCallsEvents>(event: K, handler: TgCallsEvents[K]): void
once<K extends keyof TgCallsEvents>(event: K, handler: TgCallsEvents[K]): () => void
```

Multiple handlers per event are supported — all run in registration order. `on`
and `once` return an unsubscribe function; `off` removes a specific handler.
`once` runs a handler a single time then removes it. A handler that throws/rejects
is logged (via `logger`) and never blocks the other handlers or crashes the process.
Registering any `streamEnd` handler suppresses auto-leave.

## Types

### `ChatRef`

```ts
type ChatRef = string | number | bigint;
```

Async methods accept a marked id (`-100…`), `@username`, or `t.me` link. Sync
`getCall()` / `isActive()` accept numeric ids or aliases previously resolved by this
client. `activeCalls()` always returns marked ids.

### `AudioSource`

```ts
type AudioSource =
  | { kind: 'file'; path: string }
  | { kind: 'url'; url: string; audioUrl?: string }
  | { kind: 'shell'; command: string };
```

### `JoinOptions`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `muted` | `boolean` | `false` | join with microphone muted |
| `autoLeave` | `boolean` | `true` | leave when the audio stream ends (suppressed by a `streamEnd` handler) |
| `allowCreate` | `boolean` | `false` | create a missing voice chat (requires admin rights) |
| `inviteHash` | `string` | — | invite hash when joining via a call invite link |
| `video` | `VideoOptions \| false` | — | share video from the same source |
| `presentation` | `boolean` | `false` | use the presentation channel for this call |

### `VideoOptions`

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `width` | `number` | probed / 640 |
| `height` | `number` | probed / 360 |
| `fps` | `number` | probed / 25 |
| `adjustByHeight` | `boolean` | `true` |

### `VideoQuality` (presets)

```ts
VideoQuality.UHD_4K   // { width: 3840, height: 2160, fps: 60 }
VideoQuality.QHD_2K   // { width: 2560, height: 1440, fps: 60 }
VideoQuality.FHD_1080p// { width: 1920, height: 1080, fps: 60 }
VideoQuality.HD_720p  // { width: 1280, height: 720,  fps: 30 }
VideoQuality.SD_480p  // { width: 854,  height: 480,  fps: 30 }
VideoQuality.SD_360p  // { width: 640,  height: 360,  fps: 30 }
```

### `JoinResult`

```ts
interface JoinResult { chatId: bigint; call: unknown; ssrc: number; }
```

### `ActiveCall`

```ts
interface ActiveCall {
  chatId: bigint; call: unknown; ssrc: number; source: AudioSource;
  videoActive: boolean; presentationActive: boolean;
  muted: boolean; autoLeave: boolean; joinedAt: number;
}
```

### `StreamEndInfo`

```ts
interface StreamEndInfo {
  chatId: bigint;
  source: AudioSource | null;
  willAutoLeave: boolean; // true when no streamEnd handler is registered and autoLeave is on
}
```

### `TgCallsEvents`

```ts
interface TgCallsEvents {
  streamEnd: (info: StreamEndInfo) => void | Promise<void>;
  connectionChange: (chatId: bigint, state: ConnectionState) => void | Promise<void>;
  update: (update: unknown) => void | Promise<void>;
}
```

`ConnectionState` is a numeric enum (from ntgcalls): `CONNECTING=1`, `CONNECTED=2`,
`FAILED=4`, `TIMEOUT=8`, `CLOSED=16`.

## Errors

All extend `TgCallsError` (which extends `Error`); `error.name` is the class name.

| Class | Extra | Thrown when |
|---|---|---|
| `TgCallsError` | — | base class for all library errors |
| `AlreadyInCallError` | `chatId: bigint` | `join`/`joinIdle` while already in a call (or mid-join) in that chat |
| `NoVoiceChatError` | — | no active voice chat and `allowCreate` not set |
| `UnrecognizedClientError` | — | the `client` is neither GramJS-family, mtcute, nor an adapter |

## Adapters

```ts
class GramjsAdapter implements MTProtoAdapter { constructor(client: MTProtoLike, opts?: { Api?: unknown }) }
class MtcuteAdapter implements MTProtoAdapter { constructor(client: MtcuteLike) }
function createAdapter(client: SupportedClient, opts?: { Api?: unknown }): MTProtoAdapter
function isAdapter(client: unknown): client is MTProtoAdapter
function isMtcuteClient(client: unknown): client is MtcuteLike
function isGramjsClient(client: unknown): client is MTProtoLike
```

`MTProtoAdapter` interface: `resolveChatId`, `getGroupCall`, `joinGroupCall`,
`leaveGroupCall`, `joinPresentationCall`, `leavePresentationCall`,
`extractConnectionParams`, `installUpdateHandler`, optional `dispose`.

## Media helpers

```ts
pcmCommand(source: AudioSource, opts: TgCallsOptions): string
audioDescription(source: AudioSource, opts: TgCallsOptions): object
videoDescription(source, video: VideoOptions, opts): object
probeVideo(filePathOrUrl: string, opts, target?: VideoOptions): Promise<{width,height,fps}>
resolveYouTube(url: string, opts, video?: boolean): Promise<string | null>
resolveYouTubeStreams(url: string, opts, maxHeight?: number): Promise<{ url: string; audioUrl?: string } | null>
```

## TL helpers

```ts
loadTl(provided?: unknown): AnyApi   // resolve/cache the raw TL namespace (telegram → teleproto)
resetTlCache(): void
loadEvents(...): unknown
```


<!-- ===== docs/troubleshooting.md ===== -->

# Troubleshooting

# Troubleshooting

## `Error: ntgcalls: no prebuilt binary for linux-x64`

Some npm versions (seen with **npm 12 installing from a git URL**) skip `ntgcalls`'
platform-specific optional dependency. Install it yourself, matching the `ntgcalls`
version in `package.json` (currently `3.0.7`):

```bash
npm install @ntgcalls/linux-x64@3.0.7 --no-save
```

Use the matching package on other platforms:

| Platform | Package |
|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `@ntgcalls/linux-x64` |
| Linux arm64 | `@ntgcalls/linux-arm64` |
| macOS arm64 | `@ntgcalls/darwin-arm64` |
| Windows x64 | `@ntgcalls/win32-x64` |

Installing from the npm registry (once published) resolves optional dependencies
normally and avoids this entirely. npm 10 (e.g. on many cloud images) installs the
binary correctly from a git URL.

## `default_launcher: No such file or directory (vfork_launcher)`

This confusing error from the native core almost always means **ffmpeg is not on
PATH**. ntgcalls spawns ffmpeg per source; without it you get a boost process-launch
ENOENT instead of a clear "ffmpeg not found".

```bash
sudo apt-get install ffmpeg     # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install ffmpeg             # macOS
ffmpeg -version                 # verify it resolves
```

The test suite now fails fast with a clear message if ffmpeg is missing.

## Join fails / kicked after ~25 seconds

On **UDP-blocked hosts** (some VPS/firewalls), a regular RTC join gets an ICE timeout
and Telegram kicks the participant after ~25s. Options:

- Use `joinIdle(chat, { allowCreate: true })` — creates the call in **RTMP-stream**
  mode and joins muted (no local media path needed). Existing calls are not converted.
- Presentation/screen share requires RTC and is **unavailable** in RTMP/STREAM mode.
- On UDP-capable hosts (verified on InstaBox/AWS), normal RTC joins and idle presence
  are stable indefinitely (40+ minutes tested).

Check outbound UDP:

```bash
timeout 5 bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/udp/stun.l.google.com/19302' && echo "UDP OK"
```

## `NoVoiceChatError`

There is no active voice chat in the target chat. Start one manually, or pass
`allowCreate: true` (the account needs admin rights to create a call).

## `AlreadyInCallError`

You called `join`/`joinIdle` while already in a call (or mid-join) in that chat.
`leave(chat)` first. The error carries `chatId`.

## YouTube: "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"

YouTube blocks **datacenter IPs** (cloud VMs) across all player clients. Fixes:

- **Cookies** from a logged-in browser (Netscape format):
  ```bash
  yt-dlp --cookies cookies.txt --js-runtimes node -f "bestvideo[vcodec~='^(vp09|avc1)']+bestaudio[ext=m4a]/best" URL
  ```
  Treat cookies as account credentials: store `chmod 600`, never log them, delete/rotate after use.
- A recent **yt-dlp** and a JS runtime (`--js-runtimes node` or deno) — extraction
  without a JS runtime is deprecated and may miss formats.
- Prefer `vp9`/`avc1` over AV1 for video (AV1 is too heavy to decode in real time on small VPS).
- Fallback: download from a residential IP, then transfer the file to the cloud host.

## Login / 2FA (teleproto)

- `client.start()` probes `updates.getState()`, which throws `AUTH_KEY_UNREGISTERED`
  on an empty session. For QR login use `client.signInUserWithQrCode(...)` directly;
  the QR token is a Buffer — encode `tg://login?token=<base64url>` for the QR image.
- For phone login, provide `phoneNumber`, `phoneCode`, and `password` (2FA) callbacks.
- Keep the resulting StringSession secret; reuse it with `new StringSession(str)` +
  `client.connect()`.

## Process aborts on exit

`process.exit()` immediately after native use can abort during WebRTC teardown
(cosmetic). `await tg.dispose()` and let queued callbacks drain before exiting;
long-running bots are unaffected.

## Mixing `telegram` and `teleproto`

Pass the matching `Api` namespace to each `TgCallsClient` to avoid ambiguous TL
auto-detection. mtcute uses its own TL schema and needs no `Api`.

## Incoming P2P call never connects (ICE `TIMEOUT`)

Four distinct failures can each stop a 1-on-1 call; the wrapper fixes them, but
they matter if you call `ntgcalls` directly or debug a fork:

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `An array was expected` from `initExchange` | `bytes::binary` is read as `Napi::Array` — `Buffer`/`Uint8Array` are rejected | pass `Array.from(buf)` |
| `phone.acceptCall` → `CALL_PEER_INVALID` | TL `long` is a `big-integer` object; `BigInt(obj)` goes through `Number` and loses precision | convert via `toString()` |
| `connectP2p` → `incomplete JSON [boost.json:3]` | `customParameters: ''` is a *present* optional; `json::parse("")` throws | pass `'{}'` |
| `Failed to parse received SCTP packet`, `Sorting 0 available connections`, then `TIMEOUT` | versions list includes `12.0.0`/`13.0.0` → ntgcalls routes signaling over an SCTP data channel, but Telegram sends it via MTProto | restrict to `8.0.0`/`9.0.0` |

Debug with `setLogLevel(LogLevel.DEBUG)` (from `ntgcalls`) and
`listenCalls({ debug: true })`. A healthy call logs, in order:
`Using signaling V2 Legacy` → `Decrypting packets` (inbound signaling) →
`new remote candidate` → `state= 2` (`CONNECTED`) →
`First audio RTP packet sent to pacer`.


<!-- ===== AGENTS.md ===== -->

# AGENTS.md (contributor notes)

# AGENTS.md

Guidance for coding agents working on **tgcalls-js**.

## What this is

A TypeScript wrapper (`src/`) around the `ntgcalls` native binding that streams
audio/video into Telegram voice chats via a GramJS-family or mtcute MTProto client.
ESM (`"type": "module"`), strict TypeScript, Node ≥ 18.

## Commands

```bash
npm install            # npm 11+ may warn "install scripts blocked" for esbuild — cosmetic
npm run build          # tsc → dist/
npm run typecheck:all  # tsc -p tsconfig.all.json (src + examples + test)
npm test               # tsx test/run.ts — offline suite, NO Telegram credentials
npm run smoke          # node smoke.mjs — verify dist/index.js exports
```

CI without GitHub Actions: `scripts/ci.sh` (npm ci → build → typecheck:all → test →
smoke; `--fresh [ref]` clones pristine first). GitHub Actions may be disabled at the
account level — prefer `scripts/ci.sh` for verification.

## Hard rules

- **Never run live joins without an explicit user-account session and permission.**
  Bots cannot join voice chats. The offline test suite is the default verification path.
- The offline suite uses a **fake MTProto client + the real ntgcalls native core** — it
  proves protocol plumbing (ssrc round-trip, cleanup, races, dispose) without login.
- `ffmpeg` must be on PATH to run `npm test`; the suite fails fast with a clear message
  if it is missing.

## Native binary pitfall

`npm install` from a git URL on some npm versions (e.g. npm 12) skips the optional
`@ntgcalls/linux-x64` package → `Error: ntgcalls: no prebuilt binary for linux-x64`.
Fix: `npm install @ntgcalls/linux-x64@3.0.7 --no-save` (match the `ntgcalls` version).

## Domain pitfalls (do not regress these)

- Join order is fixed: getFullChannel → createCall → setStreamSources → joinGroupCall
  → connect. The same join-params string goes to JoinGroupCall; its ssrc is reused for
  LeaveGroupCall.
- `setStreamSources` REPLACES all devices — omitting the video channel drops it.
  `setSource()` must rebuild video. Camera and screen cannot be active simultaneously.
- `streamEnd` fires once per playback; with video, wait for BOTH audio and video to end
  before auto-leave.
- A failed join must stop the native call and send LeaveGroupCall (no zombie participant).
- mtcute TL `Long` (low/high) objects must be preserved by reference — do not convert to
  bigint. GramJS/teleproto use plain bigint.
- `ConnectionState` is numeric (CONNECTING=1, CONNECTED=2, FAILED=4, TIMEOUT=8, CLOSED=16).
- On native CLOSED/FAILED, leave via MTProto BEFORE notifying listeners.

## Conventions

- Library errors extend `TgCallsError` (`src/errors.ts`); add new typed errors there.
- Internal warnings go through `opts.logger` (default `console.error`) — do not
  `console.log` directly from library code.
- Public API is re-exported from `src/index.ts`; keep `src/types.ts` the source of truth
  for shared types. Examples live in `examples/`, tests in `test/`.
- Examples use `teleproto` (the maintained GramJS fork); runtime still supports `telegram`.
- Docs: `README.md`, `docs/*.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`. Keep them in sync with the
  public API when you change signatures.

## Release

Version in `package.json` + a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Tag `vX.Y.Z` and
`gh release create vX.Y.Z` (releases via gh API work even when Actions is disabled).


<!-- ===== CHANGELOG.md ===== -->

# CHANGELOG

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Feat: **outgoing P2P calls** — `callUser(userId, { video })` places a 1-on-1 call
  and streams the configured `source` into it (mic + optional camera), reusing the
  same transport/recording path as incoming calls. Verified live.
- Feat: **video + audio recording of a 1-on-1 call** (`record: { path }`), muxed to
  mp4 with ffmpeg; audio-only recording also available.
- Fix: `phone.requestCall` result is wrapped (`{ phoneCall, users }`) — the call id
  was read from the wrapper and came out as `0`.
- Fix: `phone.confirmCall` has no `gB` field; the adapter now sends `gA` and a raw
  `Buffer` (the native-facing `jsBytes()` array is wrong for MTProto).

## 0.7.1 (2026-11-20)

- Fix: **`connectionChange` now reports the final state** — after a peer hangs up
  (or `stopListeningCalls()` runs) consumers received no transition, so state maps
  stayed stuck on `CONNECTED` (2). `P2PCallManager` emits `ConnectionState.CLOSED`
  (16) for each torn-down peer. Covered by an offline test.
## 0.7.0 (2026-11-20)

**P2P calls now work end-to-end — verified live** (ICE `CONNECTED`, audio RTP flowing,
caller hears the stream). Four defects were fixed on the way; all were silent or
misattributed, so they are documented here.

- Fix: **byte parameters must be JS arrays** — the ntgcalls N-API glue reads
  `bytes::binary` via `v.As<Napi::Array>()`, so `Buffer`/`Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer`
  throw `An array was expected`. New `jsBytes()` helper converts at every binding
  boundary (`initExchange` p/random/gaHash, `exchangeKeys` gAOrB, `sendSignalingData`,
  `RTCServer.peerTag`). The published `index.d.ts` claiming `Buffer` is wrong.
- Fix: **64-bit TL integers were lossy** — teleproto represents `long` as a
  `big-integer` object; `BigInt(obj)` goes through `valueOf()` → `Number` and loses
  precision above 2^53, so `accessHash` was corrupted and `phone.acceptCall` returned
  `CALL_PEER_INVALID`. New `asBigInt0()` converts via `toString()`.
- Fix: **`connectP2p` customParameters** — `''` is a *present* optional, so the native
  `json::parse("")` threw `incomplete JSON`. Now sends `'{}'`.
- Fix: **signaling version selection** — ntgcalls picks the highest supported version
  from the list; `12.0.0`/`13.0.0` select `SignalingSctpConnection` (signaling over the
  SCTP data channel), but Telegram 1:1 calls carry signaling over MTProto. Inbound
  packets were fed into SCTP (`Failed to parse received SCTP packet`), remote candidates
  never reached ICE, and the call timed out with `Sorting 0 available connections`.
  Now restricted to the peer's V2 subset (`8.0.0`/`9.0.0`).
- Feat: `listenCalls({ debug: true })` for per-step signaling/ICE diagnostics; the
  verbose `[p2p]` logs are off by default.
- Docs: P2P marked verified; implementer notes on arrays, V2 signaling and `debug`.

## 0.6.0 (2026-11-19)

> **Superseded by 0.7.0** — the blocker described below was a binding-usage issue,
> not an upstream bug: byte arguments must be plain JS arrays. P2P works in 0.7.0.

> **⚠️ P2P calls are EXPERIMENTAL and not yet functional live.** The signaling
> orchestration is implemented and offline-tested, but actual calls are blocked by
> an ntgcalls **JS-binding** bug: `initExchange` throws `An array was expected`
> when converting `DhConfig` (`std::vector<byte>`) — reproduced with Buffer /
> Uint8Array / Array / ArrayBuffer / DataView inputs, on ntgcalls 3.0.7 **and**
> 3.1.0-beta01. The Python/Go bindings accept the same inputs. Needs an upstream
> ntgcalls fix before P2P works end-to-end. Group-call features are unaffected.

- Feat: **multi-handler events** — `on()` now supports multiple handlers per event
  (all run in registration order) and returns an unsubscribe function; new `off()`
  and `once()`. A throwing handler no longer blocks the others. Previously the last
  registration won. Non-breaking for single-handler use.
- Feat (experimental): **incoming P2P (1-on-1) voice calls** — `listenCalls({ source, autoAccept?, onIncoming? })`,
  `stopListeningCalls()`, `activeCallPeers()`. Answers incoming Telegram voice calls
  and streams an audio source into them. The DH key exchange and WebRTC engine run
  in the ntgcalls native core; the library orchestrates the MTProto signaling
  (`phone.acceptCall` / `sendSignalingData`, `UpdatePhoneCall` / `UpdatePhoneCallSignalingData`),
  including signaling queueing before connect and clean teardown on discard.
- Adapter: new optional P2P methods on `MTProtoAdapter` (getDhConfig/acceptCall/
  requestCall/confirmCall/discardCall/sendSignalingData/installCallHandler/resolveUserId),
  implemented for GramJS/teleproto. New `P2PCallManager` + `ListenCallsOptions` exports.
- Scope: incoming calls only this release; outgoing calls and multi-party conference
  are follow-up phases. Requires a GramJS/teleproto client (mtcute P2P not yet wired).
- Docs: P2P section in guide + API reference; `examples/call-gramjs.ts`.

## 0.5.0 (2026-11-19)

- Feat: call recording — `startRecording(chat, path, opts?)`, `stopRecording(chat)`,
  `getRecording(chat)`, `isRecording(chat)`. Records **incoming** call audio:
  ntgcalls mixes all remote speakers (its native `ThreadedAudioMixer`) and pipes
  s16le PCM to ffmpeg, which encodes to `path` (container from the extension:
  `.wav` / `.mp3` / `.opus`). Options: `sampleRate` (default 48000), `channels`
  (default 1). Stopping SIGTERMs ffmpeg so the container finalizes cleanly.
- New types: `RecordOptions`, `RecordingInfo`; new media helper `recordingDescription()`.
- Docs: recording section in the guide + API reference; `examples/record-gramjs.ts`.

## 0.4.0 (2026-11-19)

- Feat: built-in playlist/queue — `play()`, `enqueue()`/`then()`, `skip()`,
  `playOnHold()`, `clearQueue()`, `getCurrent()`, `getQueue()`. Tracks advance
  automatically when each one ends; a hold track loops while the queue is empty.
  The call only auto-leaves when the queue **and** hold are empty. `skip()` with
  nothing queued pauses playback (the call stays open).
- Non-breaking: the lower-level `setSource()`/`join()` and the manual `streamEnd`
  queue pattern still work unchanged.
- Docs: playlist section in the guide + API reference; new `examples/playlist-gramjs.ts`.

## 0.3.1 (2026-11-18)

- Fix: typed errors — new `TgCallsError` base plus `AlreadyInCallError`,
  `NoVoiceChatError`, `UnrecognizedClientError` (with `chatId` where
  applicable) replace bare `Error` throws, so consumers can `instanceof`
  instead of matching message strings. All still extend `Error`.
- Feat: `logger` option on `TgCallsOptions` — route the library's internal
  warnings (e.g. a throwing event handler) into your own logger. Defaults to
  `console.error` (previous behaviour).
- Fix: test suite now fails fast with a clear message when `ffmpeg` is not on
  PATH (previously the missing binary surfaced from ntgcalls as a confusing
  `vfork_launcher` ENOENT crash).
- Chore: dev dependency `telegram` (archived GramJS) replaced by its maintained
  fork `teleproto`; examples updated. Runtime support for `telegram` is
  unchanged.
- Docs: install troubleshooting for the native binary on npm versions that
  skip optional dependencies, and the ffmpeg PATH requirement.

## 0.3.0 (2026-11-10)

- Feat: Add support for mtcute (`@mtcute/node`, `@mtcute/core`) via modular `MTProtoAdapter` and automatic client detection.
- Feat: Export `MtcuteAdapter`, `GramjsAdapter`, `createAdapter`, `isMtcuteClient`, and `isGramjsClient`.

- Fix: `setSource()` no longer drops the camera/screen video channel (ntgcalls removes any device omitted from `setStreamSources`); the video is rebuilt from the new source.
- Fix: `streamEnd` fires once per playback. With video active it waits for both audio and video to end (was: once per stream type, auto-leaving early).
- Fix: a failed `join()` now stops the native call and sends `LeaveGroupCall` (no zombie participant).
- Fix: an event handler that throws/rejects no longer crashes the process (logged instead).
- Fix: `joinYouTube()` with video/presentation now requests separate `bestvideo[height<=720]+bestaudio` streams (new `resolveYouTubeStreams()`, `audioUrl` on url sources) instead of the low-res pre-merged format that looked blurry.
- Perf: video scaling `lanczos` -> `bicubic` (lighter on small VPS).
- `startPresentation()`: skips the empty idle audio source; marks camera inactive (ntgcalls can't mix camera and screen).

## 0.2.0 (2026-09-08)

- Video sharing: `join(..., { video: {width, height, fps} })`
- Screen share: `startPresentation()` / `stopPresentation()`
- `joinIdle()` for stable idle presence

## 0.1.0 (2026-09-08)

First release. Audio-only.

- `join()` / `joinYouTube()` with file / URL / shell PCM sources
- `setSource()` — swap track without leaving (queue support)
- `pause` / `resume` / `mute` / `unmute` / `leave` / `time`
- Events: `streamEnd`, `connectionChange`, `update`
- Works with GramJS (`telegram`) and teleproto; offline test suite with fake
  MTProto + real ntgcalls native core
